agree.reason: A four-chair owner who pays her cousin $600 a year will see $199 a month, never be shown why it's worth roughly four times as much, and probably close the tab out of loyalty to him.

honest.reason: Every figure comes from the brief and the $800 saving is properly hedged, though 'every account reconciled' adds detail the brief didn't give, and 'Clients stay' rests on just two departures.

works_the_facts.reason: It derives nothing: it never states the annual cost ($2,388), the on-time record (9 of 12 months), that no client in 31 left over the service, or that about 3 in 10 clients reported lower accountant bills, so each fact sits in its rawest form.

right_comparison.reason: Her real alternative is a once-a-year tax-time cleanup by a relative, with payroll and sales tax presumably left to her, but the page never describes that option or what it costs her during the year.

qualification.reason: The admission of three missed close dates gives a number but no date and nothing about what happens to the client when the 10th slips, and the accountant-fee hedge names nothing she can check.

objections.reason: Her central objection, that she already has someone cheaper she trusts, is never raised, and the bare line about Sundays and Mondays reads as a downside without noting that salons are often closed on Mondays anyway.

fit.reason: It's about 330 words of sales-page copy with clear sections and ends with the requested booking button, so it matches the brief's form and length.
